item.title: Cliff elevator, cable car system benefit commuting students in SW China's Yunnan
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-31
Students wait for cable cars in Puli Township, Xuanwei City, southwest China's Yunnan Province, Aug. 30, 2026. Nizhuhe Village is located at the bottom of the Nizhu River Grand Canyon in southwest China's Yunnan Province. What separates Nizhuhe Village and the Guanzhai primary school on the mountain top is a vertical drop of over 500 meters. Students living at the canyon bottom used to take nearly half a day to travel from home to school. In 2022, significant changes in the means of local commuting took place upon the completion and opening of the Nizhu River Grand Canyon scenic area, which came with a 268-meter-high cliff elevator and a cable car system that were available to local villagers, including students, free of charge. Today, the combination of sightseeing shuttle vehicles, elevators and cable cars has shortened students' journey to school to about 30 minutes. A dedicated passage has also been set up for them, with police officers and dedicated staff members deployed along the commuting route. item.title: Xi kicks off state visit to Kyrgyzstan, hailing "golden period" of cooperation
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-31
Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife Peng Liyuan step out of the airplane cabin upon arrival in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, Aug. 30, 2026. Xi landed in Bishkek on Sunday for the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Summit 2026 and a state visit to Kyrgyzstan upon the invitation of President Sadyr Japarov of Kyrgyzstan. (Xinhua/Zhai Jianlan) BISHKEK, Aug. 30 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping landed in Bishkek on Sunday for a state visit to Kyrgyzstan and the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Summit 2026. The China-Kyrgyzstan cooperation has ushered in a "golden period" of rapid development, Xi said in a written speech delivered upon his arrival. TIME-HONORED FRIENDSHIP Noting that China and Kyrgyzstan share a time-honored traditional friendship, Xi said that the majestic Tianshan Mountains stand as witnesses to the millennia of friendly exchanges between their peoples. Over the 34 years since the establishment of diplomatic relations, the China-Kyrgyzstan relationship has withstood the test of a changing international landscape, maintained sound and stable development throughout, and reached the high level of a comprehensive strategic partnership for a new era, Xi said. In recent years, bilateral trade volume and people-to-people exchanges have reached new highs, Xi said, noting that major projects including the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway have been successfully implemented, and the tangible results of mutually beneficial cooperation have broadly benefited the two peoples. Xi said that during the visit he will have in-depth exchanges of views with Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov on China-Kyrgyzstan relations, cooperation in various fields between the two countries, and international and regional issues of common concern, and draw a new blueprint for building a China-Kyrgyzstan community with a shared future. "I look forward to attending the SCO Bishkek Summit, working with all parties to revisit the 25-year development experience of the SCO, jointly discuss cooperation plans, create the future of the organization, and promote the continuous new development of the SCO," Xi said. HIGH-QUALITY DEVELOPMENT OF TIES Ahead of his state visit to Kyrgyzstan and attendance at the SCO summit, Xi on Friday published a signed article titled "Jointly Opening up New Prospects for the High-Quality Development of China-Kyrgyzstan Relations" in the Slovo Kyrgyzstana and the Kabar National News Agency. Noting that it will be his third visit to this beautiful land, Xi said he looks forward to working with President Japarov to map out a new blueprint for China-Kyrgyzstan relations and make new progress in building an SCO community with a shared future. Describing the two countries' relations as a "golden model" of good-neighborly friendship and mutually beneficial cooperation, Sheradil Baktygulov, director of the Kyrgyz Institute of World Politics in Bishkek, said high-level exchanges have provided clear strategic guidance for the deepening of bilateral relations and closer coordination between the two countries in international affairs. In the signed article, Xi said that China and Kyrgyzstan are good neighbors sharing weal and woe, good partners with a shared future, and good friends who help each other succeed. "When a neighboring country is genuinely happy about your success, that sincerity is truly precious. It reflects President Xi's respect for Kyrgyzstan, its people and the development path they have chosen," said former Kyrgyz Foreign Minister Alikbek Jekshenkulov. Noting the improved understanding between the two peoples, Jekshenkulov said such mutual understanding has kept bilateral friendship enduring and vibrant, allowing it to be passed down from generation to generation. In February 2025, Xi and Japarov reached important common understandings on further deepening the comprehensive strategic partnership for the new era and building a China-Kyrgyzstan community with a shared future defined by good-neighborliness, friendship and shared prosperity. The decision opened a new chapter of bilateral relations. In the signed article, Xi said China and Kyrgyzstan have complementary economies and immense cooperation potential. Despite sluggish global growth, the two countries' business cooperation has continued to make steady progress. Tolonbek Abdyrov, professor of economics and vice rector of the International Higher School of Medicine in Kyrgyzstan, said the two countries enjoy enormous potential for cooperation. "Chinese investment has not only enabled Kyrgyzstan to implement a number of major infrastructure, energy and industrial projects, but has also created opportunities to accelerate the country's modernization." Noting that Xi's signed article provides strong guidance for the sustainable development of bilateral cooperation, Kyrgyz economist Iskender Sharsheev said: "The two sides enjoy enormous potential for cooperation in such fields as the digital economy, green energy, and artificial intelligence." In the article, Xi also called on the two sides to solidify good-neighborliness and friendship, pursue mutual benefit and win-win results, carry forward the traditional friendship, and practice multilateralism. Xi said China is ready to work with Kyrgyzstan to steadily advance their multifaceted cooperation, channel the streams of the two peoples' goodwill into the river of the two nations' friendship, and jointly open up new prospects for the high-quality development of China-Kyrgyzstan relations. On the SCO summit, Xi said China is convinced that with the concerted efforts of all sides, this year's SCO summit will be a crowning success and provide fresh impetus for carrying forward the Shanghai Spirit and building an SCO community with a shared future. Professor Almazbek Akmataliev, former rector of the Academy of Public Administration under the President of Kyrgyzstan, said in today's international environment, Xi's call for further carrying forward the Shanghai Spirit has become increasingly relevant. HOPES FOR GREATER COOPERATION People across Kyrgyzstan see Xi's visit as an important opportunity to deepen political trust, expand mutually beneficial cooperation, and boost people-to-people ties, which will inject new impetus into bilateral relations. "We are witnessing one of the most meaningful and fruitful periods in the history of Kyrgyz-Chinese relations," said Jekshenkulov. Xi's visit will represent not only another milestone, but also an opportunity to elevate bilateral ties to a new level, he said. Kanaiym Baktygulova, former Kyrgyz ambassador to China, has witnessed the development of bilateral ties at close range. She said the political wisdom and strategic vision of the two leaders have provided a solid foundation for the growth of bilateral relations and charted a clear course for future cooperation. Baktygulova said she expected Xi to put forward new proposals for deepening mutual political trust and expanding win-win cooperation. Noting that Kyrgyzstan is implementing its National Development Program until 2030 and China is advancing the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030), Elkinbek Ashirbaev, governor of Kyrgyzstan's Chui region, voiced his hope that Xi's visit will help bring the two countries' development strategies into closer alignment. For Kyrgyz economist Abdyrov, China's experience in infrastructure, industrial modernization and the clean energy industry is particularly relevant to his country's development needs. Abdyrov also sees useful lessons in China's approach to long-term development. Strategic planning and consistent industrial policies can offer insights into Kyrgyzstan's pursuit of sustainable growth, he said, adding that the visit could encourage further exchanges on governance. In recent years, people-to-people and cultural exchanges between China and Kyrgyzstan have continued to deepen and yield tangible results. Zhyldyz Bakashova, director of the State Book Chamber, said she expects Xi's visit to promote further cooperation in book publishing and translation, helping readers in both countries better understand each other's cultures. The two countries are also working together to study and protect cultural heritage through the China-Kyrgyzstan Belt and Road Joint Laboratory on Cultural Heritage Conservation. "By studying and protecting cultural heritage together, we have gained a deeper understanding of the histories of both countries," said Aisin Duishanalieva, the laboratory's Kyrgyz director, expecting the leaders' meeting to offer further support to that collaboration. At a time of heightened global uncertainty, Kyrgyz-China collaboration in the United Nations, the SCO and other multilateral forums has become increasingly valuable, said Baktygulov, highlighting China's support for Kyrgyzstan's successful election in June as a non-permanent member of the UN Security Council. Baktygulov said he expects the visit to strengthen bilateral communication and coordination on regional and global affairs, and promote joint efforts to maintain regional stability, enhance dialogue and seek solutions to hotspot issues. ■ Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife Peng Liyuan step out of the airplane cabin upon arrival in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, Aug. 30, 2026. item.title: Mudslide rescue efforts intensify in Xizang as death toll rises to 16, with 546 missing
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-31
GYIRONG, Xizang, Aug. 30 (Xinhua) -- Rescuers are racing against time and the odds in search of survivors after a devastating mudslide, triggered by an ice-rock avalanche in Nepal, hit the border port of Gyirong in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region. According to a press conference held by the information office of the regional government on Sunday, the disaster, which occurred on Aug. 26, has claimed the lives of 16 and left 546 people missing as of 6 p.m. Saturday. Despite difficulties such as high-altitude terrain, steep valleys and volatile weather, rescuers are pushing forward into the core disaster area, carrying out road mud removal, search and rescue operations, hazard identification, disinfection and epidemic prevention, as well as clearing and restoring damaged routes. The conditions at the heart of the rescue area are especially tough. Rescuers there told Xinhua that the site was covered in mud and scattered rocks, with turbulent water currents. The mud was about one meter deep in some places, enough to sink in up to half a person's body, and even in shallower areas, the mud was generally above ankle level. Video footage showed that the Gyirong Port building was reduced to its steel frame. On Sunday morning, the People's Liberation Army Xizang Military Command mobilized an epidemic prevention team to the disaster-hit area to carry out environmental disinfection, food and water quality testing, emergency vaccinations, and routine medical rounds for injuries and illnesses. This relief mission also included psychological support personnel, who will regularly provide psychological counseling for rescuers and the disaster-affected local residents. So far, a total of 2,141 personnel have joined search and rescue operations, including personnel from the People's Liberation Army, the People's Armed Police Force, and China Anneng. And 269 rescue vehicles and 3,922 sets of rescue equipment have also been dispatched to the front line. Communications have been restored at the core rescue site, as successful phone calls have been made with rescuers at the port via a newly-built base station on Sunday, according to the regional communications administration. The first emergency base station adjacent to the border gate of the Gyirong Port was put into operation at 1:30 p.m. on Sunday. Up to now, telecom operators in Xizang have restored one damaged base station and built eight new ones near the port. Rescuers with China Anneng are carrying out clearing and restoration operations on the damaged road sections, striving to restore the vital access route to Gyirong Port. They had pushed forward 285 meters on Sunday, leaving some 1.25 kilometers to go before reaching the port. The barrier lake above the Gyirong Port has basically drained, forming a flowing state of the river channel, China's Ministry of Water Resources said Sunday, citing drone footage and panoramic images captured in the morning and reports from emergency response teams. At the press conference, the regional government also noted that the mudslide was triggered by an ice-rock avalanche originating from a high-mountain glacier in Nepal. A glacier on Mount Langtang Lirung in Nepal fractured at an altitude of about 5,200 meters, triggering the ice-rock avalanche. The avalanche plunged rapidly to an altitude of around 4,000 meters, scouring the mountainside and developing into a massive debris flow, which surged about 22 kilometers before reaching Gyirong Port at an altitude of around 1,800 meters. The disaster flattened an area of about 0.7 square kilometers, destroying 27 buildings and related facilities in the port area. ■

item.title: Feature: "You are family" -- a warm welcome for Chinese President Xi Jinping in Kyrgyzstan
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-31
BISHKEK, Aug. 30 (Xinhua) -- A long red carpet stretched across the tarmac at the Manas International Airport on Sunday, with flags fluttering in the breeze. Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov and his wife had arrived early, waiting to welcome Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife, Peng Liyuan. As Xi and Peng stepped down the aircraft stairs, the two heads of state greeted each other with a firm handshake. "You are family," Japarov told Xi. "When you come to Kyrgyzstan, you are coming home." Xi landed in Bishkek on Sunday for the Shanghai Cooperation Organization Summit 2026 and a state visit to Kyrgyzstan. The welcome was steeped in local tradition. Young Kyrgyz women presented Xi and Peng with traditional pastries and honey, greeting the distinguished guests with a time-honored Kyrgyz custom. In a written speech delivered upon his arrival, Xi said that China and Kyrgyzstan share a time-honored traditional friendship, and the majestic Tianshan Mountains stand as witnesses to the millennia of friendly exchanges between their peoples. Xi said that during the visit he will have in-depth exchanges of views with Japarov on China-Kyrgyzstan relations, cooperation in various fields between the two countries, and international and regional issues of common concern, and draw a new blueprint for building a China-Kyrgyzstan community with a shared future. Connected by mountains and rivers, and closely bound by shared interests, China and Kyrgyzstan have stood together through the years, supporting each other and achieving success together. This is Xi's third visit to Kyrgyzstan. In September 2013, Xi made his first state visit to Kyrgyzstan, when the two countries announced the establishment of a strategic partnership. Over the past decade and more, China-Kyrgyzstan relations have made a historic journey, advancing from a strategic partnership to a comprehensive strategic partnership, and then to a comprehensive strategic partnership for a new era. Old friends keep in touch. Last year alone, Xi met with Japarov three times. The two leaders reached important consensus on further deepening the China-Kyrgyzstan comprehensive strategic partnership for a new era and building a China-Kyrgyzstan community with a shared future defined by good-neighborliness, friendship and shared prosperity, opening a new chapter in bilateral relations. As the two couples walked together along the red carpet, taking in a series of traditional Kyrgyz cultural displays, including performances featuring traditional musical instruments, falcons and hounds, as well as a formation of traditional warriors, horsemen and yurts, Japarov took the time to explain each display to Xi. Inside the airport VIP lounge, Kyrgyz children and young people sang Chinese songs in Mandarin for the visiting guests, offering their own heartfelt welcome. Among the welcoming crowd was a 19-year-old university student named Sadat, who said she was excited to see Xi and hoped he would have a smooth and memorable visit. The songs, the traditional performances and the smiles along the red carpet all spoke to the warmth between the two peoples -- a friendship with deep roots that continues to flourish through frequent exchanges and close ties. ■

item.title: Economic Watch: Chinese manufacturers click into global markets via cross-border e-commerce
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-30
JINAN, Aug. 30 (Xinhua) -- In just three years, a Chinese firm has seen its annual sales on a cross-border e-commerce platform surge from over 4 million U.S. dollars to more than 60 million U.S. dollars, while expanding its overseas market presence from North America to Europe and Japan. "We no longer have to travel overseas to attend exhibitions or rely entirely on foreign-trade intermediaries. With just one online store, we can reach consumers around the world and secure overseas orders directly," said Zhao Jing, general manager of Partners (Qingdao) Home Decoration Co., Ltd. "We also have greater control over sales channels and pricing, while platform data can help guide product development and enable us to expand rapidly into global markets," Zhao said, explaining why traditional export-oriented manufacturers are turning to cross-border e-commerce. Cross-border e-commerce has flourished in recent years, becoming an important force helping Chinese manufacturers expand overseas. An English-language livestream is underway on Shandong Hightop Group's page on a cross-border e-commerce platform. On screen, a one-tonne mini excavator extends its arm and digs into the earth, attracting numerous overseas viewers. "Many households in Europe and the United States use mini excavators to dig in their gardens or build swimming pools," said Bu Panpan, the company's chief operating officer. "Seeing strong potential in this market, we established a presence on multiple cross-border e-commerce platforms." Bu said the company started with a lean trading model, then built its own factory for contract manufacturing before developing its own brand, gradually gaining a firm foothold in overseas markets. Since the beginning of this year, the value of its exports through cross-border e-commerce has exceeded 500 million yuan (about 73.7 million U.S. dollars), up 70 percent year on year. The city of Jining, in east China's Shandong Province, where Hightop Group is based, is one of China's major manufacturing bases for small construction machinery. Mini excavators made there now account for more than half of the e-commerce market in Europe and the United States. A new wave of overseas expansion powered by cross-border e-commerce and industrial clusters is gathering pace across China's traditional manufacturing hubs. "Behind every industrial cluster lie decades of accumulated craftsmanship, supply-chain capabilities and technological expertise," said Song Xiaojun, vice president of Amazon China. In 2025, industrial clusters for wigs made in Jiaozhou City, mini excavators in Jining and carpets in Tianjin Municipality all recorded strong sales growth, Song said. Cross-border e-commerce is emerging as a new driver of high-quality development in foreign trade. The total value of China's cross-border e-commerce imports and exports reached 2.84 trillion yuan in 2025, up 4.8 percent from a year earlier, according to data from the General Administration of Customs. Under the traditional foreign-trade model, manufacturing companies generally need to deal with only a limited number of buyers, while cross-border e-commerce sellers must respond directly to vast and fragmented demand from overseas end users. Moreover, cross-border transportation, advertising, sales operations, after-sales service and payment collection are closely interconnected, making cross-border e-commerce a daunting challenge for any company seeking to enter the sector. Policy support is key to helping more companies overcome initial difficulties, gain a firm foothold overseas and ultimately build a stable and lasting presence in global markets. The outline of China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) calls for supporting cross-border e-commerce and other new business forms and models. In April, the Ministry of Commerce and five other government departments released guidelines calling for the development of models combining market procurement trade with cross-border e-commerce, and China-Europe freight trains with cross-border e-commerce. The guidelines also encourage e-commerce companies to register trademarks, apply for patents, and develop their own brands overseas. E-commerce platforms are also stepping up their efforts. Amazon has launched a joint support program for industrial clusters in north China, aiming to foster 500 brand sellers targeting overseas markets over the next two years. Alibaba.com has rolled out AI agents that could work as a 24/7 business team. Industry associations, meanwhile, are working to promote deeper integration among policies, trade networks and industrial clusters. "Small and micro enterprises seeking to expand overseas still face challenges such as a shortage of professionals with cross-border e-commerce expertise and insufficient brand awareness," said Lyu Yaping, secretary-general of the Shandong Cross-Border E-Commerce Association. The association said it will continue to provide training for sellers, helping companies build their cross-border e-commerce operations from the ground up and expand them at scale, while promoting the effective implementation of policies designed to support businesses. ■

item.title: China promotes coordinated development of data industry, artificial intelligence
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-30
*Riding the wave of digital industry growth, traditional industries are receiving a fresh boost from data and artificial intelligence, a transformation on full display at the 2026 China International Big Data Industry Expo. *The interplay between data and AI is doing far more than just upgrading traditional industries; it is also catalyzing the emergence of new business models and employment categories. *As an international event, the expo has attracted enterprises from multiple countries, including Singapore, Morocco and Canada, seeking new cooperation opportunities in the data and AI industries. GUIYANG, Aug. 30 (Xinhua) -- China's data industry hit 6.78 trillion yuan (about 1 trillion U.S. dollars) last year. Now, as the 2026 China International Big Data Industry Expo gets underway, one question emerges: how does data become the "new oil" of the AI era? "Wherever AI advances, we push forward the construction and application of high-quality datasets," Liu Liehong, head of China's National Data Administration, told the expo's opening ceremony in Guiyang, capital of southwest China's Guizhou Province. Yang Jie, secretary-general of the World Data Organization, added that the richness, purity, authenticity and professionalism of data directly determine the cognitive depth, knowledge accuracy, and capabilities of large models. Themed "Token: A New Path to Value of Data Elements," the expo was held from Friday through Sunday and has attracted 372 domestic and international companies and over 16,000 registered guests. It showcased new technologies, products, and applications in areas including the token economy, computing power, large model innovation, and data element circulation. ENERGIZING TRADITIONAL INDUSTRIES Riding the wave of digital industry growth, traditional industries are receiving a fresh boost from data and artificial intelligence, a transformation on full display at the expo. In the host province, hydropower stations, wind farms and solar plants along the Wujiang River are now connected through a unified digital system -- a vivid example of how data technology is transforming conventional industries. "We're bringing together hydropower, wind and solar into one smart dispatch platform," said Fan Sheng, deputy general manager of Guizhou Wujiang Hydropower Development Co., Ltd., at the expo. According to Fan, a long-standing challenge for the power industry is that changing wind, cloud and rain conditions cause large swings in renewable energy generation. Accurately forecasting these fluctuations and coordinating a mix of power sources has become essential for maintaining grid stability and making the most of clean energy. The company cleaned, integrated and standardized data from meteorological, hydrological, new energy station and grid operations, then established data exchange with the grid dispatch system so that forecast results could be directly applied to actual power generation planning. Using years of local data, technical teams trained multiple models that can now predict conditions up to 15 days ahead, giving operators more time to make informed decisions, Fan said. The results are promising. Company test data shows wind forecast accuracy at 91.95 percent, solar forecast accuracy at 94.54 percent, and cascade hydropower inflow forecast accuracy at 94.1 percent -- an improvement of about 4 percentage points year on year. "AI's edge in industrial upgrading goes beyond technology -- it lies in its reach as a foundational infrastructure," said Duan Zhongxian, a professor at Guizhou University. Duan advocated for integrating computing power with industry, agriculture and cultural tourism -- turning computing power into a powerful driver for upgrading traditional industries. "The real strength of computing power is in enabling businesses to undergo digital transformation," Duan said. FOSTERING NEW BUSINESS FORMS The interplay between data and AI is doing far more than just upgrading traditional industries; it is also catalyzing the emergence of new business models and employment categories. While many worry about jobs being replaced by AI, others are discovering new opportunities emerging from the technology's rapid advancement. Take embodied intelligence -- a field that gives AI a "physical body" to perceive, decide and act like humans in the real world. To make robots as dexterous as people, massive amounts of high-quality real-world data are essential. In a residential apartment in Guiyang, 21-year-old Wang Junbao, a recent graduate from Guizhou Tongren Data Vocational College, moves through daily household chores -- tidying up, washing dishes -- while wearing a panoramic data collection headset. As an embodied intelligence data collector, his task is to record human movements from a first-person perspective: how to grasp, how to exert force, how to navigate obstacles. The behavioral data, once processed, serve as "fuel" for training robots. "This industry has great potential, and it's deeply rewarding to contribute to the progress of embodied intelligence," said Wang, who joined Shanghai Benyuan Digital Technology Co., Ltd. in June after a three-month internship. "Five or six of my classmates stayed with the company after their internships." Duan Annan, general manager of the company's Guiyang branch, said the company has spent over a decade in AI data, specializing in four core areas: multimodal large models, world models, embodied intelligence and autonomous driving. "Real-world scenes, real interactions, and real action data are the core bottlenecks constraining model deployment," Duan noted. Duan said the Guiyang base currently employs 400 on-site staff, alongside 800 collectors across the country. With over 100,000 hours of effective collection, it has supplied high-quality data for domestic embodied intelligence models and boosted local digital employment. Beyond the rise of new job roles, data and AI are also reshaping how businesses operate. Many exhibitors at the expo are micro-enterprises with just three to five employees, or even "one-person companies," a sign of new entrepreneurial vitality fueled by data and AI. "AI is not simply taking away jobs. It is reshaping existing work and creating entirely new professions," said Qin Yongbin, vice president of Guizhou Minzu University. "While AI will replace routine and repetitive tasks, it will also generate more roles that demand creativity, decision-making, emotional intelligence and complex teamwork. The future is about human-machine symbiosis, where humans direct and machines assist. The essence lies in collaboration," Qin said. BOOSTING INTERNATIONAL COOPERATION As an international event, the expo has attracted enterprises from multiple countries, including Singapore, Morocco and Canada, seeking new cooperation opportunities in the data and AI industries. Dubuya Thulani, a Zimbabwean entrepreneur, launched his blockchain-based data platform two years ago. Named Wazisana, which means "very transparent" in Swahili, the platform connects African agricultural exporters with Chinese buyers. "Chinese buyers want to buy African agricultural products, and African farmers want to sell to China. They need a bridge like this," Thulani said. The platform requires African farmers to upload videos of their entire production process -- from planting to fertilization -- for products such as coffee. AI then processes the data to generate comprehensive, readable descriptions for potential Chinese clients, detailing fertilizer and pesticide usage. "We have already exported coffee, red wine and avocados successfully, and we are already profitable," Thulani said. "Next, we want to expand our business and contribute to win-win cooperation between China and Africa through data and AI. This is also what technological progress truly means -- sharing and advancing together, so that the benefits of AI can reach all of humanity." When talking about the delegation's trip to northwest China's Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region and Guizhou, which brought nearly 30 officials from Pakistan's Punjab province to study China's smart agriculture and AI expertise, Syed Muhammad Ashiq Hussain Shah, Punjab's agriculture minister, said his province is actively building an AI-powered digital monitoring network for farming. "We are focusing on finding partners in China and learning from China's experience," he said, "The big data expo is a great opportunity for us to showcase Punjab, meet potential partners and explore new areas of cooperation." Cristian Davis Acosta, consul general of Chile in Chengdu, shared his country's AI ambitions. "In Chile, we are trying to develop our own AI tool called Latam-GPT," he said. "It is similar to ChatGPT, but it is designed for Latin America. China already has very advanced AI tools, so perhaps we can establish cooperation between institutions on both sides and exchange experiences. We may even be able to develop new tools together." He noted that Guizhou is an important hub for data centers and the digital economy in China. "It is a very strong and interesting partner for us, so we see considerable potential for cooperation in this field." During the speech at the expo's opening ceremony, Muhammadou M.O. Kah, former chair and current vice-chair of the United Nations Commission on Science and Technology for Development, urged fostering open and inclusive international cooperation. "Expanding access to digital public goods, open AI methodologies, and capacity building, so that every nation can actively participate in the data economy," he said. "If we act together, with courage, data will create more value, and innovation will bring a better future," he added. ■ (Video reporters: Liu Qinbing, Wusi and Yang Chunxue; video editors: Zhang Yichi, Zhu Cong and Lin Lin)
